title: Transient Expression in Red Beet of a Biopharmaceutical Candidate Vaccine for Type-1 Diabetes
protocol: Grow red beet (B. vulgaris cv Moulin Rouge) plants in a growth chamber under 150 µE of light intensity, 65% relative humidity, and a 12 h light/dark cycle at 23/21 °C.
Fertilize the red beet plants twice a week with a 1 g/L solution of commercially available fertilizer after seed germination.
Grow spinach (S. oleracea cv Industria) in a growth chamber under 150 µE of light intensity, 65% relative humidity, and a 12 h light/dark cycle at 23/21 °C.
Fertilize the spinach plants twice a week with a 1 g/L solution of commercially available fertilizer after seed germination.

Introduce the plant expression vectors - the 5’ module (pICH20111), the 3’ modules (pICH31070.GAD65mut, pICH31070.∆87G65mut and pICH7410.eGFP), and the integrase module (pICH14011) - into Agrobacterium tumefaciens GV3101 strain using standard techniques.
Grow Agrobacterium cultures on LB medium containing 50 μg/mL rifampicin and appropriate vector-specific antibiotics for 2 days at 28 °C.
Screen colonies by colony PCR using primers: 5’-ATCTAAGCTAGGGTACCTCG-3’ and 5’-ACACCGTAAGTCTATCTCTTC-3’ for vectors pICH31070.GAD65mut and pICH31070.∆87G65mut.
Set annealing temperature to 55 °C and elongation time to 110 s for the first set of primers.
Use primers: 5’-TGAAGTTCATCTGCACCAC-3’ and 5’-ACACCGTAAGTCTATCTCTTC-3’ for vector pICH7410.eGFP.
Set annealing temperature to 53 °C and elongation time to 30 s for the second set of primers.
Use primers: 5’-AATGTCGATAGTCTCGTACG-3’ and 5’-TCCACCTTTAACGAAGTCTG-3’ for the 5’ module.
Set annealing temperature to 53 °C and elongation time to 20 s for the third set of primers.
Use primers: 5’-GGCAACCGTTATGCGAATCC-3’ and 5’-GATGCGTTCCGCAACGAACT-3’ for the integrase module.
Set annealing temperature to 57 °C and elongation time to 45 s for the fourth set of primers.
Carry out PCR reaction in a total volume of 20 μL.
Perform initial denaturation at 95 °C for 5 min.
Cycle through 35 cycles, each consisting of 30 s at 95 °C, annealing temperature and elongation time specific to each primer couple.
Conclude with a final elongation step of 7 min at 72 °C.
Inoculate the three A. tumefaciens transformants in 50 mL of LB medium containing 50 μg/mL rifampicin and vector-specific antibiotics.
Grow by shaking overnight at 28 °C.
Pellet overnight bacterial cultures by centrifugation at 4,500 x g for 20 min.
Resuspend pellets in infiltration buffer containing 10 mM MES (pH 5.5) and 10 mM MgSO4.
Incubate the suspensions at room temperature for 3 h.
Mix equal volumes of bacterial suspensions containing GAD65mut, ∆87GAD65mut or eGFP 3’ module with 5’ module and integrase module.
Use the suspension mix for syringe infiltration of red beet and spinach leaves.
Place 5 mL of the suspension in a syringe without the needle.
Press the tip of the syringe against the underside of the leaf for both spinach and red beet plants.
Infiltrate the first three completely expanded leaves starting from the apex for each plant.
Label the agroinfiltrated leaves with a paper tag on the leaf stem.
Return the plants to a growth chamber under standard conditions.
Collect agroinfiltrated leaves from 4 to 14 days post infection (dpi).
Freeze collected leaves in liquid nitrogen.
Store frozen plant tissue at -80 °C.
Grow A. tumefaciens transformants in LB medium containing rifampicin and appropriate vector-specific antibiotic.
Centrifuge overnight bacterial cultures at 4,500 x g for 20 min.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 L of infiltration buffer to an OD600 of 0.35.
Incubate suspensions at room temperature (RT) for 3 h.
Add 0.01% v/v polysorbate 20 to each suspension.
Mix equal volumes of bacterial suspensions containing GAD65mut, ∆87GAD65mut or eGFP 3’ module with 5’ module and integrase module.
Insert a six-week-old red beet plant in the holder.
Invert the holder and place it on top of a beaker containing the infiltration bath to submerge the leaves in bacterial suspension.
Ensure all leaves are completely dipped in the bacterial suspension.
Transfer the infiltration bath with the submerged plant to the infiltration chamber and close it.
Turn on the vacuum pump and open the vacuum intake valve on the infiltration chamber.
Keep the vacuum until pressure in the infiltration chamber reduces to 90 mbar.
Maintain the vacuum for 3 min at 90 mbar.
Release the vacuum for 45 s.
Return the infiltration chamber to atmospheric pressure.
Open the chamber and remove the infiltrated plant from the bacterial bath.
Place the plants back in a growth chamber under standard conditions.
Collect agroinfiltrated leaves at the maximum expression dpi and freeze them in liquid nitrogen.
Store collected plant tissue at -80 °C.
Grind syringe or vacuum-infiltrated red beet and spinach leaves to fine powder in liquid nitrogen using mortar and pestle.
Transfer the powdered leaf material into 15 mL plastic tubes and store at -80 °C.
Add 900 µL of extraction buffer (50 mM sodium phosphate pH 8.0, 20 mM sodium metabisulphite) to 300 mg of leaf powder.
Vortex the mixture for 1 min to homogenize.
Centrifuge the mixture at 30,000 x g for 40 min at 4 °C.
Collect and store the supernatant in a clean tube at -80 °C.
Load 100 µL of each TSP extract obtained from eGFP expressing leaves, in three technical replicates, on a 96-well plate.
Put the 96-well plate in a fluorescence reader and start the measurement using the 485/535 nm filter set.
Mix 50 parts of Reagent A with 1 part of Reagent B to prepare the BCA working solution.
Pipette 0.1 mL of each standard (including a blank) into labelled tubes.
Add 1.9 mL of BCA working solution and mix thoroughly for each sample.
Cover the tubes and incubate at 37 °C for 30 min.
Cool the tubes to RT.
Measure the absorbance at 562 nm of all samples within 10 min.
Transfer proteins onto a nitrocellulose membrane using standard techniques.
Prepare the blocking solution by mixing 4% milk in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) pH 7.4.
Block the membrane with 10 mL of the blocking solution at room temperature for 1 hour.
Incubate the membrane with rabbit primary antibody solutions overnight at 4 °C or for 4 hours at room temperature with constant agitation.
Discard the primary antibody and wash the membrane three times for 5 minutes each with blocking solution containing 0.1% detergent.
Prepare the horseradish peroxidase (HRP)-conjugated anti-rabbit antibody at 1:10,000 in blocking solution with 0.1% detergent.
Incubate the membrane for 1.5 hours at room temperature with constant agitation.
Discard the secondary antibody and wash the membrane 5 times for 5 min each with PBS-T.
Incubate the membrane with a commercially available luminol solution following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Detect the signal using a chemiluminescence imaging system.
Harvest vacuum agroinfiltrated ∆87GAD65mut-expressing red beet leaves at the expression peak (11 dpi).
Freeze the harvested leaves in liquid nitrogen and lyophilize them for 72 h at -50 °C and 0.04 mbar.
Store the lyophilized leaves at -80°C.
Grind the frozen leaves to fine powder and store it at RT in a sealed container with silica gel.
Weigh 100 mg of grinded freeze-dried red beet leaves and resuspend them in 6 mL of PBS (pH 7.4).
Adjust the sample pH to 2 with 6 M HCl.
Add 4 mg/mL pepsin from porcine gastric mucosa in 10 mM HCl to obtain a final concentration of 1 mg/mL or a ratio of 1:20 to total soluble proteins.
Shake the sample at 37 °C for 120 min.
Adjust the samples to pH 8 with 1 M NaOH to inactivate pepsin.
Centrifuge 750 µL aliquots of each sample at 20,000 x g for 20 min at 4 °C.
Collect the supernatant separately and resuspend the pellet in one volume of loading buffer.
Prepare two samples of 100 mg of grinded freeze-dried red beet leaves.
Resuspend both samples in 6 mL of PBS (pH 7.4).
Adjust the pH of only one sample to 2 with 6 M HCl.
Shake both samples at 37 °C for 120 min.
Centrifuge 750 µL aliquots of each sample at 20,000 x g for 20 min at 4 °C.
Collect the supernatant separately and resuspend the pellet in one volume of loading buffer.
Analyze both the supernatant and the resuspended pellet by western blot analysis.
Weigh 100 mg of freeze-dried red beet leaves.
Resuspend the powder in 8 mL of sterile PBS (pH 7.4) and vortex for 1 min.

Prepare the LB medium without antibiotics or containing 50 µg/mL rifampicin, 50 µg/mL each of rifampicin and carbenicillin, 50 µg/mL each of rifampicin and kanamycin, or 50 µg/mL each of rifampicin, carbenicillin, and kanamycin.
Plate 1 mL of the freeze-dried leaf homogenate in one of the 5 selective LB media.
Incubate all plates for 3 days at 28 °C.
Count Agrobacterium colonies on each plate.
Calculate residual bacterial charge as CFU per mL of freeze-dried leaf homogenate.
Weigh 30 mg of vacuum agroinfiltrated ∆87GAD65mut-expressing red beet leaf powder in a 2 mL plastic tube.
Add 750 μL cold methanol/chloroform (70/30 v/v) to the leaf powder and vortex for 30 s.
Incubate at -20 °C for 2 h.
Add 600 μL cold water to the mixture and centrifuge at 17,900 x g at 4 °C for 10 min.
Collect and transfer the upper hydroalcoholic phase into a new 2 mL tube.
Discard the lower chloroformic phase and interphase.
Evaporate solvents from samples using a vacuum concentrator for 3 h.
Dissolve the pellet in 300 μL acetonitrile/water (50/50 v/v) and sonicate for 3 min.
Pass solutions through 0.2 μm membrane filters and place into transparent fixed 300 μL insert glass tubes.
Weigh 300 mg of vacuum agroinfiltrated ∆87GAD65mut-expressing red beet leaf powder in a 15 mL plastic tube.
Add 3 mL methanol to the leaf powder and vortex for 30 s.
Sonicate at 40 kHz for 15 min.
Centrifuge samples at 4,500 x g at 4 °C for 10 min.
Transfer supernatants into new 15 mL tubes.
Dilute 100 µL of extract 1:3 (v/v) with water.
Pass the diluted solution through a 0.2 μm membrane filter.
Put the filtered solution into a transparent fixed 300 µL insert glass tube.
Weigh 200 mg of -80 °C stored, vacuum agroinfiltrated ∆87GAD65mut-expressing red beet leaf powder in a 15 mL plastic tube.
Add 200 μl of water to the weighed leaf powder.
Add 2 ml of methanol to the mixture.
Keep on ice for 1 h.
Vortex for 30 s.
Sonicate at 40 kHz for 15 min.
Centrifuge the samples at 4,500 x g at 4 °C for 25 min.
Collect and transfer the chloroform phase into 2 ml tubes.
Discard the upper hydroalcoholic phase and the interphase.
Put the samples into a vacuum concentrator for 3 h to evaporate the solvent.
Dissolve the pellet obtained with 600 μl of methanol.
Dilute 100 μL of extract 1:5 (v/v) with methanol.
Pass the diluted solution through a 0.2-μm membrane filter.
Put the filtered solution into a transparent fixed 300 µL insert glass tube.
Prepare appropriate solvents for the HPLC gradients for primary metabolite analysis using 20 mM ammonium formate as solvent A and 95% acetonitrile, 5% water plus 10 mM ammonium formate as solvent B.
Prepare appropriate solvents for the HPLC gradients for secondary metabolite analysis using water plus 0.05% formic acid (A) and acetonitrile plus 0.05% formic acid (B).
Prepare appropriate solvents for the HPLC gradients for polar lipid analysis using water plus 0.05% formic acid (A) and 100% acetonitrile (B).
Use gradients from Table 1 for metabolite elution.
Set flow rate at 0.2 mL/min.
Inject 10 μL of each sample for secondary metabolites and polar lipids.
Inject 5 μL of each sample for primary metabolites.
Prepare a quality control (QC) sample by mixing equal portions of different samples.
Analyse the QC sample during the experiment to monitor instrument efficiency.
Insert a QC sample analysis after every 10 sample-batch.
Randomize the order of samples to avoid instrument-driven effects.
Perform a column cleaning method and a blank analysis after every 9 analyses.
The blank consists of an injection of pure methanol: water (50/50, v/v).
Set up the instrument to acquire mass spectra in alternate positive and negative ionization modes using parameters listed in Table 2.
